L0: Thousands of satellites, one sky. Won't they crash into each other? Plot twist: they follow three rules.
L1: Level one! Fly low. Starlink orbits below six hundred kilometres. Up there, thin air still drags satellites down. If a satellite breaks, it sinks. Gone in five years or less, even if nobody steers it. Low orbits clean themselves. No dead junk circling forever. Steady!
L2: Every satellite has a forecast of where it will be. That forecast is called an ephemeris. Starlink shares its forecasts publicly.
L3: Level two! Get out of the way. Forecasts cross? Its thrusters steer it clear. Stargaze: thirty thousand sensors on Starlink watch for other objects up there. Spot it, share it, dodge it. Power!
L4: Boss level! Leave nothing behind. Old satellite? Deorbit it: steer it down on purpose. Built to burn up in the air on the way down. Aimed over open ocean. Brought down early if a part might fail. Safe out there and on the way down.
L5: Fly low. Get out of the way. Leave nothing behind. A safe sky is a shared sky. Space safe!
